id_and_class.theory_title: Cooke’s Nondual Naturalism and Living Mirror Theory
id_and_class.summary: James Cooke argues that consciousness is the epistemic relation between a living organism and its world, arising wherever matter organizes itself into a self-maintaining living system. His Living Mirror Theory grounds this in predictive modeling and the free energy principle, and his Nondual Naturalism places it in a process-relational reality with no fundamental substances, which he says dissolves the hard problem.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as the Epistemic Dimension of Life

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is epistemic relationality: the knowing interface by which a living organism tracks and adapts to the conditions, including its own body, that keep it alive.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Mind and matter are two aspects of one relational process. Cooke rejects grounding reality in any substance, whether matter, mental essence, or pure awareness, and treats the mind-body gap as a product of substance thinking.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Emergence with life: consciousness appears necessarily wherever matter forms self-persisting systems that maintain their boundaries and resist entropy.
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Subjectivity is the organism’s point of view in its relation to the world, and directedness follows from the organism modeling what it needs to persist. Cooke treats the sense of a separate, enduring self that ‘has’ experiences as an illusion.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Cooke identifies awareness itself, an open, formless epistemic space in which contents arise and pass, as the main thing to explain. Particular qualities are contents within that relational space rather than properties of a substance.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Interdependent processes and relations rather than independent substances; living, self-organizing systems; predictive models of the environment.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Neuroscience and the physics of life, combined with contemplative and mystical experience, which Cooke treats as genuine insight into nonduality rather than delusion.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Living organisms in relation to their environment, with brains as modifiers of a capacity rooted in life itself; awareness as the space within which experiential contents appear.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal awareness, the self (deflated as a constructed separateness), and the origin and distribution of consciousness across living things.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Organisms persist by minimizing entropy through predictive modeling of their environment, and this self-maintaining modeling is the epistemic interface that constitutes consciousness.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Consciousness began with the origin of life and persists as an ongoing process of prediction and updating in every living thing. Brains elaborate and modify it in animals like us.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Between the organism and the world rather than inside the head; present in all living things, since all life must model its conditions to persist.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Consciousness is the means by which organisms track and adapt to the conditions that sustain them, so it is part of life’s self-maintenance.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Drawing on predictive processing, the organism continuously generates predictions about its world and updates them to reduce error.
mechanism_and_dynamics.evolutionary_account: Life and mind share one origin: when matter first organized into self-persisting systems, consciousness appeared with them, and nervous systems later elaborated it.
core_claims_and_evidence: Reality consists of interdependent processes rather than independent substances, a view Cooke links to the Madhyamaka teaching of emptiness.
The hard problem is a symptom of mistaken assumptions about separation and substance rather than a real mystery.
Because all living things must predictively model their environment to persist, all living things possess experiential awareness.
Mystical experiences of unity reveal awareness itself when the constructs of self, separation, and substance dissolve.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical and theoretical, drawing on predictive processing and free energy neuroscience, the biology of self-organization, and contemplative phenomenology.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Extending experiential awareness to all life, including single cells and plants, goes well beyond what predictive modeling alone shows. The framework also sits between labels, calling itself naturalistic and a neutral monism while treating mystical insight as evidence.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: It remains open why predictive self-maintenance should be experiential at all, and how to tell which systems count as alive and therefore conscious.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Internally consistent as a process-relational neutral monism, though placing it under materialism is a loose fit given its rejection of matter as a fundamental substance.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Since consciousness arises from being alive rather than from computation, an artificial system would be conscious only if it were a genuinely self-maintaining living system.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Consciousness here is the epistemic side of an organism’s self-maintenance, so it ends when that living process ends. Cooke treats the fear of death as fed by the illusion of a separate self.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Meaning comes from recognizing that humans belong to the web of life rather than standing apart from it, which Cooke ties to ecological ethics rather than cosmic teleology.

virtual_immortality.rationale: Uploading would copy a computation, but Cooke denies that consciousness is a computation performed by a brain.
